judgment: for the great person, good; no harm.
Words are spoken and not believed.
image: The marsh has no water: Hemmed In.
So the noble one stakes his life
lines: His buttocks are hemmed in on a tree stump.
He goes down into a dark valley:
three years, and he sees nothing.
He is hemmed in at wine and food,
but the scarlet knee-covers are coming.
It is good to use offering and sacrifice.
To march: misfortune, yet no harm.
He is hemmed in by stone,
and leans on thorns.
He goes into his own palace —
and does not see his wife. Misfortune.
He comes slowly, slowly,
hemmed in by a metal carriage.
Shame, but there is an end to it.
His nose is cut, his feet cut off,
and he is hemmed in by scarlet knee-covers.
Then, slowly, there is release.
It is good to use sacrifice.
He is hemmed in by vines, on ground that shakes.
He says: if I move, I will regret it.
But if he regrets, and marches: good.

notes.name_en: 困 is being boxed in on all sides (a tree in a box); 'Hemmed In', not Wilhelm's 'Oppression'.
notes.L2: 朱紱/赤紱 scarlet ritual knee-covers = the officer come with relief; kept as the garment.
